items.q: In the urine chloride ladder, ‘low’ urine chloride is defined as:
items.exp: Urine chloride < 25 mEq/L is the ‘low’ band; > 40 mEq/L is the ‘normal’ band of the ladder. (Book p825)

items.q: Match the urine-chloride band to its meaning — 1) Low (< 25 mEq/L)  2) Normal (> 40 mEq/L)  3) High … A) ECF volume expansion  B) GI loss, post hypercapnia, cystic fibrosis, late diuretics  C) Renal loss — diuretics (early phase), Bartter, Gitelman
items.exp: Low urine Cl⁻ (< 25 mEq/L): GI loss, post hypercapnia, cystic fibrosis and diuretics in the late phase. Normal (> 40 mEq/L): ECF volume expansion. High: renal loss — diuretics in the early phase, Bartter syndrome, Gitelman syndrome. (Book p825)

items.q: Which conditions appear in the LOW urine-chloride band of the ladder?
opts: GI loss, post hypercapnia, cystic fibrosis, diuretics (late phase)
GI loss, cystic fibrosis, diuretics (early phase), Bartter syndrome
ECF volume expansion plus Bartter and Gitelman syndrome
Renal loss from diuretics (early phase) and cystic fibrosis only
items.exp: Low urine chloride: GI loss, post hypercapnia, cystic fibrosis and diuretics in the late phase. (Book p825)

items.q: A patient is on diuretics and has an alkalosis. Why does the urine chloride differ between the early and late phase of diuretic use?
opts: Early diuretic use lies in the high-chloride renal-loss band, while late-phase use falls into the low-chloride band
Early diuretic use lies in the low-chloride band, while late-phase use lies in the high band
Both phases always fall in the low-chloride band
Urine chloride is uninterpretable once diuretics are started
items.exp: The ladder prints diuretics under the high urine chloride (early phase) renal-loss column but also under the low band as diuretics (late phase). (Book p825)

items.q: Which two tubulopathies are printed in the HIGH urine-chloride column of renal loss?
items.exp: High urine chloride renal loss: diuretics (early phase), Bartter syndrome and Gitelman syndrome. (Book p825)

items.q: ‘In the urine chloride ladder, a normal urine chloride (> 40 mEq/L) points to ECF volume expansion.’
opts: True — that band is labelled ECF volume expansion
False — the normal band is labelled renal loss
False — the normal band is labelled GI loss
True, but only in the presence of hypertension
items.exp: Normal urine chloride: > 40 mEq/L — ECF volume expansion, i.e. the saline-unresponsive group. (Book p825)

items.q: All but one of these are printed in the LOW urine chloride band. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Bartter syndrome belongs to the high urine-chloride renal-loss column with Gitelman syndrome and early-phase diuretics. (Book p825)

items.q: A patient with metabolic alkalosis has a urine chloride of 12 mEq/L. Which pair of explanations is printed for this band?
opts: GI loss or diuretics in the late phase
ECF volume expansion or Bartter syndrome
Diuretics in the early phase or cystic fibrosis
items.exp: A urine chloride < 25 mEq/L sits in the low band: GI loss, post hypercapnia, cystic fibrosis and diuretics (late phase). (Book p825)
